source_text: θρώπινα, καὶ ἐξωφανῆ τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐντοσθίων, τουτέστι, τῶν κεκρυμμένων αὐτοῦ μυστηρίων τὸν οἰκεῖον ἀναπιμπλάντες νοῦν, εὐτροφίαν ἕξομεν τὴν πνευματικήν. Δαπανᾶσθαί γε μὴν αὐτῇ δεῖν ἔφη τῇ μιᾷ νυκτὶ τὸν ἀμνὸν, οὐδενὸς τὸ σύμπαν περιλελειμμένου, καὶ εἰς τὸ πρωῒ μένοντος. Συντρίβεσθαι δὲ καὶ ὀστοῦν οὐκ ἐᾷ, τοῦ μὲν πρώτου κατασημαίνοντος, ὡς εἰς αἰῶνα τὸν μέλλοντα, καθ' ἕτερόν τινα τρόπον ἁγιάσει τε καὶ εὐλογήσει Χριστὸς τοὺς ἀνακειμένους αὐτῷ διὰ πίστεως καὶ ἁγιασμοῦ, καὶ οὐχὶ δὴ πάντως ἀποθρέψει πάλιν τῇ ἰδίᾳ σαρκὶ, καὶ ζωοποιήσει τῷ αἵματι, καθάπερ ἀμέλει καὶ νῦν, ἀλλ' ὡς ἤδη κατηργημένου θανάτου, καὶ λυθείσης εἰσάπαν τῆς φθορᾶς, νοητὸς ἔσται τις ὁ τοῦ ἁγιάζοντος τρόπος. Οὐκοῦν τὸ πρωῒ κατασημήνειεν ἂν οὐχ ἕτερον οἶμαί τι, παρὰ τὸν αἰῶνα τὸν μέλλοντα. Τοῦ δὲ δευτέρου, τοῦ μὴ χρῆναι, λέγω, συντρίβεσθαι τὸ ὀστοῦν, εἰς ἐννοίας ἡμᾶς ἀναφέροντος τὰς ἐπὶ Χριστῷ, καὶ ἀκολουθεῖν ἀναπείθοντος ταῖς τῶν θεηγόρων φωναῖς. Ὁ γάρτοι θεσπέσιος εὐαγγελιστὴς, σωματικώτερον ἐκλαβὼν ἐπὶ Χριστοῦ τὸ χρησμῴδημα, «Οὐ κατέαξαν αὐτοῦ,» φησὶν, «οἱ στρατιῶται τὰ σκέλη, ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ γεγραμμένον· Καὶ ὀστοῦν οὐ συντριβήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.» Ἐσθίουσι δὲ τὸν ἀμνὸν, διεζωσμένοι τὰς ὀσφύας, ὑποδησάμενοι τοὺς πόδας, καὶ βακτηρίας ἔχοντες ἐν ταῖς χερσὶ, καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς εἰπεῖν, ἐν σχήματι γεγονότες τῶν ὁδοιπορεῖν εἰωθότων, καὶ μάλα ὀρθῶς. Εὐτρεπεῖς γὰρ ὥσπερ γεγονότες τοῦ μεθίστασθαι νοητῶς, καὶ οἱονεί πως ἐξοδοιπορεῖν ἐπειγόμενοι τῶν ἐν τῷδε τῷ κόσμῳ περισπασμῶν, καὶ εἰς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἀρίστων μεταφοιτᾷν προθυμούμενοι, μεταληψόμεθα τοῦ Χριστοῦ πανάγνως καὶ καθαρῶς. Οὐ γὰρ τοῖς προσκαίροις ἐμφιλοχωρεῖν εἰθίσμεθα, μετατρέχομεν δὲ γεννικῶς εἰς τὰ πεπηγότα καὶ μένοντα· καὶ τῶν σαρκικῶν ἀκαθαρσιῶν ἀπαίροντες, εἰς ἀστειότητα τὴν πνευματικὴν μεταθρώσκομεν μεμνημένοι λέγοντος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, «Ἐγείρεσθε, ἄγωμεν ἐντεῦθεν.» Ταύτῃ τοι περίκεινται σχῆμα τοῖς ὁδοιπορεῖν εἰωθόσι τὸ πρέπον, οἱ τὸν ἀμνὸν ἐσθίοντες εἰς τύπον Χριστοῦ. Πλὴν, ἐν σπουδῇ φάγεσθαι χρή. Πάσχα γάρ ἐστι Κυρίου, τουτέστι, διάβασις, ἤτοι διαβατήρια· καιροῦ γὰρ ἐνεστηκότος καθ' ὃν ἀναγκαῖον διαβαίνειν ἡμᾶς ἐκ φαυλότητος κοσμικῆς, ἐπὶ τὸ δρᾷν ἐπείγεσθαι τὰ ἁνδάνοντα τῷ Θεῷ, τὸ μὴ ἐν ὅλῃ ταυτὶ ποιεῖσθαι σπουδῇ, διαμέλλειν δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ ἀναδύεσθαι τοῖς ἀρχαίοις ἡμᾶς προστετηκότας ἔτι κακοῖς, πῶς οὐκ ἂν εἴη τῶν σφαλερωτάτων; Καὶ γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, «Τρέχετε,» φησὶν, «ἵνα καταλάβητε.» Ἰτέον δὴ οὖν εἰς μετάληψιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ διὰ πίστεως, παντὸς μὲν ὄκνου πεπατημένου, μελλησμοῦ δὲ οὐδενὸς παρεισδεδυκότος, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν ὅλῃ σπουδῇ. Διαβησόμεθα γὰρ οὕτως ἐξ ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς δικαίωσιν, ἐκ θανάτου πρὸς ζωὴν, καὶ τὸ τῆς δουλείας αἶσχος ἀποτριψάμενοι, τὴν εὐκλεᾶ τῆς υἱοθεσίας καταπλουτήσομεν χάριν.
pass_a_gloss: (not only the hu)man and outwardly-appearing things of Emmanuel, but also filling our own mind with the very inward parts, that is, his hidden mysteries, we will have the spiritual good nourishment. And he said the lamb must be spent in the one night itself, nothing at all having been left over and remaining until morning. And he does not allow even a bone to be broken: the first signifying that in the coming age Christ will sanctify and bless in some other manner those devoted to him through faith and sanctification, and will not altogether nourish again with his own flesh and make alive by the blood, as indeed also now, but, death having already been abolished and corruption wholly dissolved, the manner of the one sanctifying will be some intelligible one. So the morning would signify, I think, nothing other than the coming age. And the second, I mean the not having to break the bone, bringing us up to the thoughts about Christ and persuading to follow the voices of the God-speakers. For the divine evangelist, having taken the oracle more bodily about Christ, says: 'The soldiers did not break his legs, so that the written thing might be fulfilled: and a bone of him will not be broken.' And they eat the lamb girded about the loins, having shod the feet and having staffs in the hands, and to say simply, having come to be in the figure of those accustomed to travel, and very rightly. For having become as it were ready to move across intelligibly, and as it were hastening to travel out from the distractions in this world, and being eager to pass over to anything whatever of the best things, we will partake of Christ all-purely and cleanly. For we are not accustomed to linger fondly among the temporary things, but we run across nobly to the fixed and remaining things; and departing from the fleshly impurities we leap across into the spiritual refinement, remembering Christ saying 'Rise, let us go from here.' For this reason those eating the lamb for a type of Christ are clothed in the fitting figure for those accustomed to travel. However, one must eat in haste. For it is the Pascha of the Lord, that is, a crossing, or crossing-rites; for a season having come in which it is necessary for us to cross from worldly baseness, to hasten to do the things pleasing to God, the not doing this in all haste, but delaying and as it were shrinking back, still melting toward the ancient evils, how would it not be among the most dangerous things? And indeed the divine Paul says 'Run so that you may grasp.' One must go then into partaking of Christ through faith, every hesitation having been trampled, and no delay having slipped in, but as in all haste. For thus we will cross from sins into justification, from death toward life, and having rubbed off the shame of slavery, we will be enriched with the renowned grace of adoption.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …human and outwardly visible in Emmanuel; but if we also fill our own mind with his very inward parts, that is, with his hidden mysteries, we shall have spiritual nourishment.

He said, moreover, that the lamb must be consumed in that one night, nothing at all being left over and remaining until morning; and he does not allow even a bone to be broken. The first signifies that in the age to come Christ will sanctify and bless those devoted to him through faith and holiness in some other way: he will surely not again nourish them with his own flesh and give them life by his blood, as he of course does now; rather, since death will already have been abolished and corruption wholly undone, the manner of the one who sanctifies will be a spiritual one. So the morning would signify, I think, nothing other than the age to come. The second, I mean that the bone must not be broken, lifts us up to the thoughts that concern Christ and persuades us to follow the voices of those who speak of God. For the inspired evangelist, taking the oracle in a more bodily sense of Christ, says: ‘The soldiers did not break his legs, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: Not a bone of him shall be broken’ (John 19:33–36).

They eat the lamb with their loins girded, their feet shod, and staffs in their hands; in short, dressed like people who are used to traveling; and very rightly. For as people made ready to move on in spirit, pressing, as it were, to travel out of the distractions of this world, and eager to pass over to whatever is best, we shall partake of Christ in all holiness and purity. For we are not used to lingering over things that pass; we run nobly toward what is fixed and abiding; and setting out from the impurities of the flesh, we leap across to spiritual refinement, remembering that Christ said, ‘Rise, let us go from here’ (John 14:31). That is why those who eat the lamb as a type of Christ wear the dress that fits travelers.

But it must be eaten in haste. For it is the Lord's Passover, that is, a crossing, or the rites of crossing. For when the time has come in which we must cross over from worldly baseness and hasten to do what pleases God, not to do this with all haste, but to delay and hang back, as it were, still clinging to our old evils, how would that not be most perilous? So the inspired Paul says, ‘Run, so that you may obtain it’ (1 Corinthians 9:24). We must go, then, to partake of Christ through faith, with all sluggishness trampled underfoot and no delay slipping in, but with all haste. For so we shall cross from sins to justification, from death to life; and rubbing off the shame of slavery, we shall be enriched with the glorious grace of adoption.
